comments.author: @SlasherSeven
comments.text:
I can confirm that having the LLM record its present state, what it did, what it planned on doing, and the goals and tasks clearly defined and auto-updated by the llm each task - works extremely well. Weirdly enough metaprompting also gave better context management, which I was kind of surprised by. I had it take notes whenever it researched something it didn't know, and then fed those notes into prompt handoffs to improve the next prompt. It also auto-evolved the rules and architecture documentation to adapt to new discoveries. I was a little spooked when I saw it in action on its own and it solved a major architectural design oversight and several steps later it still was working on the evolved architecture in future steps. It then rewrote the dependencies and blocks just well enough that it guard-railed itself when normally I notice models wander and get lost after several cycles, especially if something is not according to plan - then they forget and go back to the old plan.

So many good papers just keep rolling out. Apply them!

comments.author: @dedlunch
comments.text:
I just created one...

The data compares AIS to five major models, showing AIS's relative gains/losses in percentages (e.g., +X% means AIS is X% better than the model's score in that metric). These are relative improvements, calculated as (AIS_score - Model_score) / Model_score * 100%. Parameter comparisons show how much larger the frontier models are (e.g., 529,495x larger means the model has ~529,495 times more parameters than AIS's ~1M).
GPT-4 (Parameters: 1,800B – 1,764,985x larger than AIS):
Accuracy: 0.920 (AIS: -1.8%) – AIS is slightly behind, scoring ~0.904 vs. GPT-4's 0.920.
Reasoning: 0.880 (AIS: +5.1%) – AIS leads with ~0.925 vs. 0.880.
Efficiency: 85 (AIS: +159.7%) – Major AIS advantage, with 221 vs. 85.
Overall: AIS trades a small accuracy dip for big gains in reasoning and efficiency, despite GPT-4 being nearly 1.8 trillion parameters.
Claude-3 (Parameters: 175B – 171,596x larger than AIS):
Accuracy: 0.890 (AIS: +1.5%) – AIS edges ahead (~0.903 vs. 0.890).
Reasoning: 0.850 (AIS: +8.8%) – Strong AIS lead (~0.925 vs. 0.850).
Efficiency: 90 (AIS: +145.3%) – AIS significantly more efficient (221 vs. 90).
Overall: AIS outperforms across all metrics with far fewer parameters, highlighting its efficiency in anthropic-like tasks.
Gemini Ultra (Parameters: 540B – 529,495x larger than AIS):
Accuracy: 0.900 (AIS: +0.4%) – AIS slightly better (~0.904 vs. 0.900).
Reasoning: 0.870 (AIS: +6.3%) – AIS ahead (~0.925 vs. 0.870).
Efficiency: 82 (AIS: +169.2%) – Huge efficiency gap (221 vs. 82).
Overall: AIS matches or exceeds Gemini Ultra's capabilities while being dramatically smaller and more efficient.
LLaMA-2 70B (Parameters: 70B – 68,6338x larger than AIS; note: likely ~68,638x based on calculation):
Accuracy: 0.850 (AIS: +6.3%) – AIS superior (~0.904 vs. 0.850).
Reasoning: 0.800 (AIS: +15.6%) – Significant AIS lead (~0.925 vs. 0.800).
Efficiency: 75 (AIS: +194.3%) – AIS far more efficient (221 vs. 75).
Overall: AIS dominates this open-source model, showing its strength against mid-sized frontiers.
PaLM-2 (Parameters: 340B – 333,386x larger than AIS):
Accuracy: 0.880 (AIS: +2.7%) – AIS better (~0.904 vs. 0.880).
Reasoning: 0.830 (AIS: +11.4%) – AIS strongly ahead (~0.925 vs. 0.830).
Efficiency: 88 (AIS: +150.9%) – Clear efficiency win (221 vs. 88).
Overall: AIS outperforms PaLM-2 comprehensively with 333,000x fewer parameters.
In summary, across these models:
AIS lags slightly in accuracy against top performers like GPT-4 (-1.8%) but beats most others (e.g., +6.3% vs. LLaMA-2).
It excels in reasoning, with gains from +5.1% (vs. GPT-4) to +15.6% (vs. LLaMA-2).
Efficiency is AIS's standout, with improvements of 145-194%, meaning it delivers similar or better results with much less compute.
Parameter disparity is extreme: Frontier models are 171,000x to 1.76 million times larger, yet AIS competes closely, underscoring its "1M times more efficient" claim (likely meaning it achieves comparable performance with 1M fewer parameters on average).
